question: As per NFHS 5, what percentage of the Indian population was deprived of drinking water during the year 2019-21?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.0732**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) conducted during 2019-21, **7.32% of the Indian population lacked access to basic drinking water facilities**.
 
• The survey highlights disparities in access to safe drinking water, particularly in rural areas compared to urban regions.
 
• NFHS-5 is a comprehensive survey conducted to assess health, nutrition, and infrastructure-related parameters across India.
 
• Access to safe drinking water is a critical indicator of public health and directly impacts the quality of life and overall development of the population.
 
• The government of India has launched various programs, like the **Jal Jeevan Mission**, to address water accessibility issues and improve water supply in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Family Health Survey (NFHS)**

 
 
• NFHS is a large-scale, multi-round survey conducted in a representative sample of households throughout India.
 
• The survey provides crucial data on health, family welfare, and other emerging issues in India.
 
• NFHS-5 was conducted between 2019 and 2021, covering all 707 districts of India.
 
 
 
• **Jal Jeevan Mission**
 
 
• Launched in 2019, Jal Jeevan Mission aims to provide functional household tap connections (FHTCs) to every rural household by 2024.
 
• The mission focuses on sustainable water supply systems through the creation of local infrastructure.
 
• It also promotes water conservation and rainwater harvesting.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Lack of Drinking Water**
 
 
• Access to unsafe water can lead to waterborne diseases like diarrhea, cholera, and typhoid.
 
• It can also affect hygiene practices, particularly in rural and underserved regions.
 
• Lack of clean drinking water disproportionately affects women and children, who are often responsible for water collection in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Safe Drinking Water Definition**
 
 
• As per WHO guidelines, safe drinking water is water that is free of contaminants, harmful chemicals, and pathogens.
 
• Safe drinking water is essential for maintaining health and preventing waterborne diseases.
